messages:
From: Alex Mercer <procurement@fluxlabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFQ: Reserved capacity footprint & pricing sensitivity to GPU costs

Mina,

Thanks for taking this. Flux Labs is evaluating a reserved capacity commitment for inference (expected steady-state: ~1.8k A100-equivalent GPU hours/day across us-west/us-east) tied to a product rollout in H1. Main ask: we need clarity on how Redwood would handle material GPU cost shocks during the contract tenor. Specifically: would you offer any pass-through, indexation, or discount-protection mechanics? Our procurement/legal team pushed back on very long fixed-price tenors without a variance-trigger.

Attached is our RFP with expected usage profile and preferred start window (Jan 2028). Can you outline options and an escalation path for price movement >10% on GPU supply pricing? Also include any standard approval timelines if we request a mid-term price reset.

Alex Mercer
Head of Procurement
Flux Labs
Attachment: Flux_RFP_Q4_2027.pdf (pdf, 412KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFQ: Reserved capacity footprint & pricing sensitivity to GPU costs

Alex —

Appreciate the RFP and the clarity on the usage profile. High level we can support three distinct approaches depending on Flux's risk allocation preference:

1) Fixed-priced reserved (12–24mo) with limited annual escalator: predictable unit price, Redwood absorbs short-term GPU market swings up to an agreed buffer. Best if Flux values cost predictability.

2) Index-linked reserved (24mo option available): base price + quarterly true-up tied to a GPU spot index (we can use a third-party market index or Redwood's internal GPU price index). Includes a cap on pass-through impact per quarter and an annual reconciliation.

3) Pilot + convertible credits (6mo pilot then convert to reserved): short-term committed capacity with surge credits and an option to convert unused credits into discounted future committed months.

I'll attach a quick options matrix (reserved-tenor-options.pdf). To be realistic about approvals: any discounts or rebate mechanics that move effective annual price >15% will need sales director + finance sign-off (Marissa is cc'd). For GPU cost variance triggers that require contract language (indexation/pass-through), we'll engage legal and need to agree on thresholds and cadence for true-ups.

Please confirm which two options you'd like fleshed out into contract language and a target start date. Happy to run a short call next week with my finance and pricing leads.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: RFQ: Reserved capacity footprint & pricing sensitivity to GPU costs

Team —

Reviewed Flux's RFP and Mina's options. A few practical guardrails from a finance/ops perspective:

- Baseline assumption: Redwood will size dedicated reserved pools on expected steady-state usage + 20% buffer for headroom. Any commitment that forces >30% over-provisioning vs actual utilization needs explicit commercial crediting.

- Trigger framework proposal (suggested):
  * Tier A (0–10% GPU cost delta vs baseline index): Redwood absorbs. No customer-facing price change.
  * Tier B (10–25% delta): Quarterly true-up; Flux receives a capped pass-through of up to 50% of the incremental GPU cost above 10%, with a max annual impact of X% of committed spend (we should compute X per deal).
  * Tier C (>25% delta): Immediate escalation to VP finance + Sales Director; options include a short-term surcharge, retroactive rebate, or conversion of credits to future months — requires exec approval.

- Approval authorities: Discounts / concessions that materially change expected annualized revenue by >15% need sign-off from Sales Director + VP Finance (Marissa). Anything >30% needs CRO/CEO escalation. Please flag expected concession levels on the deal worksheet.

- Practical contract language: We should avoid open-ended pass-throughs. Use a defined third-party GPU spot index or Redwood's published index, a 30-day lookback for quarterly true-up, and caps per quarter. Legal will need time to validate force majeure and supply-chain exception language.

Attached a starter trigger table (gpu-cost-trigger-table.csv) and a link to the HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.redwood/deals/DEAL-8471). Karthik — can you run an initial scenario calc (12mo vs 24mo) and add a recommended max cap per quarter? Ben — please flag any capacity allocation constraints for Jan 2028 start.

Marissa
VP, Finance — Commercials
Redwood Inference

Subject: Consolidated proposal: reserved capacity tenor & variance-trigger options (Flux Labs)

Alex —

Thanks for the RFP and the time so far. Per your ask, attached is a consolidated commercial proposal with three concrete options and the escalation path we discussed. Short summary below:

Option A — 12-month fixed reserved (predictable):
- Unit price locked for 12 months with an annual escalator floor of 3% and Redwood-absorbed GPU price delta up to 10%.
- Overage: billed at a predefined overage rate with monthly reconciliation.
- Use case: teams wanting cost certainty and minimal contract complexity.

Option B — 24-month index-linked reserved (share risk):
- Base price + quarterly true-up tied to Redwood GPU Index (30-day lookback).
- Tiered pass-through (see trigger table): Flux bears 50% of deltas between 10–25%; >25% requires escalation with capped remedies.
- True-ups applied quarterly with annual cap (5% of committed annual spend).

Option C — 6-month pilot -> convertible credits:
- Short pilot with committed baseline and surge credits; unused committed hours convert to credits at a 60% rate toward future reserved commitments within 9 months.
- Lower up-front commitment, good for feature ramp.

Commercial notes: discounts beyond 15% will require Sales Director + VP Finance approval; material contract language around pass-throughs and caps will require legal sign-off (we can provide redlines within 5 business days once Flux selects the preferred option).

Next steps:
- Please indicate 1st and 2nd preference by EOD Thu, Oct 7.
- If you prefer Option B, we should schedule a short calibration call (30m) with Karthik to agree on baseline index and with Legal to draft the trigger language.

Proposed meeting slots: Wed 10/6 10:00–10:30 PDT, Thu 10/7 13:00–13:30 PDT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if useful.

Regards,
